## Welcome

In lesson 5 we saw that, upon differentiation, the monocytes of patients and controls change thousands of genes, and that the changes look very similar. But "looking similar" is not "being the same". In this lesson we ask the question statistically: **are there genes whose change from monocyte to dendritic cell is different in lupus patients?** To answer it we will use an **interaction model**, which directly compares the contrasts of both groups.

**What you need to know beforehand:** you should have completed the lesson [Differentiation of monocytes into dendritic cells](l5_DEGs_monocytes_diff_en.html).

**By the end you will be able to:**

1. Explain what an **interaction** is and why it is described as a "difference of differences".
2. Fit a `~ Group + Cell_type + Group:Cell_type` model with `DESeq2` and interpret its coefficients.
3. Visualize an interaction with a line plot.
4. Summarize genes by their Reactome **specific process**.
5. Reproduce **panels A and B of Figure 7** of the article.
6. Interpret an interaction using each group's **expression trajectories**.

**Estimated time:** 1.5 hours.

## Glossary

These are the terms we will use. Come back here whenever you need to.

- **Contrast**: a comparison between two conditions; for example, moDC against monocyte.
- **Interaction**: occurs when the effect of one factor depends on another. Here, when the change from monocyte to dendritic cell (factor `Cell_type`) depends on whether the person is a patient or a control (factor `Group`).
- **Difference of differences**: the value of an interaction. It is the change in patients minus the change in controls.
- **Coefficient**: each number a model estimates; `DESeq2` lists them with `resultsNames()`.
- **Specific process**: among all the enriched terms in which a gene appears, the one with the **fewest** genes; the most concrete.
- **Expression trajectory**: how a gene's mean expression changes across the differentiation stages (monocyte → moDC → tolDC) in each group.

```{r lesson_overview, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Visual summary of lesson 7."}
knitr::include_graphics("img/lesson7_overview_en.png")
```

## 1. Setup

```{r setup}
library(GeneExprLupusMx) # package data
library(tidyverse)       # table manipulation and plots
library(ComplexHeatmap)  # heatmaps
library(circlize)        # color scales for ComplexHeatmap
library(cowplot)         # combining plots into panels

# Large package objects: downloaded only the first time (see ?download_data)
filtered_txi <- download_data("filtered_txi")
zscore_mat   <- download_data("zscore_mat")
```

Colors and threshold (the same as in the previous lessons, plus those for the lists in this lesson):

```{r colores}
cell_color       <- c(monocyte = "black", moDC = "palevioletred", tolDC = "gold1")
group_color      <- c(Ctrl = "#96d4ccff", SLE = "#b493b4ff")
expression_color <- c(UP = "firebrick3", DOWN = "dodgerblue3")
comparison_color <- c(SLEvsCtrl_moDC = "#4daf4a", SLEvsCtrl_tolDC = "#ff7f00")
lfc_color        <- colorRamp2(c(-5, -1, 0, 1, 5), c("darkblue", "dodgerblue", "white", "red", "darkred"))

padj_threshold <- 0.05
```

## 2. **Step 1:** what is an interaction?

Let us take an interferon-stimulated gene, `ISG15`. In lesson 5 we calculated its LFC from monocyte to dendritic cell in each group:

```{r isg15_lfc}
sapply(de_celltype_results, function(df) round(df$log2FoldChange[df$gene == "ISG15"], 2))
```

`ISG15` goes down upon differentiation in both groups, but in patients it goes down **more**: in moDCs, −3.41 versus −1.69. The difference between those two changes is the **interaction**:

$$\text{interaction} = \text{LFC}_{\text{SLE}} - \text{LFC}_{\text{Ctrl}} = -3.41 - (-1.69) = -1.72$$

A line plot makes it evident. We plot the mean z-score of each group in each cell type, using the `zscore_mat` checkpoint:

```{r plot_interaction_fun}
plot_interaction <- function(gene) {
  metadata_cleaned %>%
    mutate(zscore    = zscore_mat[gene, as.character(sample_ID)],
           Cell_type = factor(Cell_type, levels = c("monocyte", "moDC", "tolDC"))) %>%
    group_by(Group, Cell_type) %>%
    summarise(mean_z = mean(zscore), se = sd(zscore) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = Cell_type, y = mean_z, color = Group, group = Group)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_z - se, ymax = mean_z + se), width = 0.1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = group_color) +
    labs(title = gene, x = "Cell type", y = "Mean z-score (± standard error)", color = "Group") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12)
}
```

```{r isg15_plot, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4}
plot_interaction("ISG15")
```

- If the two lines were **parallel**, the gene would change the same way in both groups: there would be no interaction.
- Here they are **not parallel**: patients start from a much higher value in monocytes (the interferon signature from lessons 2 and 3) and drop more upon differentiation.

::: {.alert .alert-warning}
**A negative interaction does not mean "lower in patients".** It means the gene **goes down more** (or goes up less) upon differentiation in patients. In the case of `ISG15`, the moDCs of both groups end up with similar levels; what changes is the slope, because patients start from a higher value.
:::

## 3. **Step 2:** the interaction model

In lesson 5 we fit one model per group and compared their LFCs "by eye". To obtain a **p-value** for the difference, we need to fit a single model with all 99 samples and an interaction term, `Group:Cell_type`:

```{r interaction_model, eval = FALSE}
library(DESeq2)

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromTximport(txi     = filtered_txi,
                                colData = metadata_cleaned,
                                design  = ~ Group + Cell_type + Group:Cell_type)
dds$Group     <- relevel(dds$Group, ref = "Ctrl")         # reference: controls
dds$Cell_type <- relevel(dds$Cell_type, ref = "monocyte") # reference: monocytes
dds <- DESeq(dds) # takes a few minutes

resultsNames(dds)
#> [1] "Intercept"                   "Group_SLE_vs_Ctrl"
#> [3] "Cell_type_moDC_vs_monocyte"  "Cell_type_tolDC_vs_monocyte"
#> [5] "GroupSLE.Cell_typemoDC"      "GroupSLE.Cell_typetolDC"
```

Each coefficient answers a different question:

| Coefficient | What does it measure? |
|-------------|-----------------------|
| `Intercept` | The baseline expression: control monocytes |
| `Group_SLE_vs_Ctrl` | SLE against Ctrl, **in monocytes** |
| `Cell_type_moDC_vs_monocyte` | moDC against monocyte, **in controls** |
| `Cell_type_tolDC_vs_monocyte` | tolDC against monocyte, **in controls** |
| `GroupSLE.Cell_typemoDC` | **Interaction:** how much the moDC-versus-monocyte difference changes in patients |
| `GroupSLE.Cell_typetolDC` | **Interaction:** the same for tolDC versus monocyte |

We are interested in the last two:

```{r interaction_results, eval = FALSE}
de_interaction_results <- lapply(c(moDC = "moDC", tolDC = "tolDC"), function(cell) {
  res <- as.data.frame(results(dds, alpha = 0.05, name = paste0("GroupSLE.Cell_type", cell)))
  data.frame(gene = rownames(res), res, row.names = NULL)
})
```

Because the model takes a while to fit, the package includes the result as a checkpoint, `de_interaction_results`:

```{r checkpoint}
names(de_interaction_results)
head(de_interaction_results$tolDC[order(de_interaction_results$tolDC$padj), ])
```

Let us check that the interaction LFC is the difference of differences we calculated by hand for `ISG15`:

```{r isg15_check}
sapply(de_interaction_results, function(df) round(df$log2FoldChange[df$gene == "ISG15"], 2))
```

In moDCs we get −1.73, practically the −1.72 we calculated by subtracting. The small difference arises because in lesson 5 the patients' model was also adjusted for disease activity and glucocorticoid dose.

## 4. **Step 3:** which genes change differently?

A gene has a significant interaction if its `padj < 0.05`. We classify it as `UP` or `DOWN` according to the sign of the LFC, and name each list `SLEvsCtrl_<direction>_<cell type>`:

```{r deg_df}
deg_df <- imap_dfr(de_interaction_results, function(df, cell) {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(padj), padj < padj_threshold) %>%
    mutate(query = paste0("SLEvsCtrl_", ifelse(log2FoldChange > 0, "UP", "DOWN"), "_", cell))
})

query_order <- c("SLEvsCtrl_UP_moDC", "SLEvsCtrl_DOWN_moDC", "SLEvsCtrl_UP_tolDC", "SLEvsCtrl_DOWN_tolDC")
dplyr::count(deg_df, query = factor(query, levels = query_order))
```

**There are very few genes**, compared with the thousands in lesson 5: almost the entire differentiation program is the same in patients and controls. And most of the interactions are **negative**: these are genes that go down more upon differentiation in patients.

Here we only require `padj < 0.05`. The LFC of an interaction is a difference between two changes, and all these genes already have differences of at least 0.34 in absolute value.

::: {.callout-note}
**Challenge 1.** How many of these genes also have a large interaction, with `|log2FoldChange| ≥ 1`?
:::

<details class="callout-tip">
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{r reto1}
deg_df %>%
  group_by(query) %>%
  summarise(total = n(), lfc_1 = sum(abs(log2FoldChange) >= 1))
```

Most of the genes in the `DOWN` lists have an interaction greater than 1: in patients, their drop upon differentiation is at least twice that in controls.

</details>

::: {.callout-note}
**Challenge 2.** Use `plot_interaction()` to plot `IL5RA` and `ABCG1`. Which cell type explains each interaction?
:::

<details class="callout-tip">
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{r reto2, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4}
plot_grid(plot_interaction("IL5RA"), plot_interaction("ABCG1"), nrow = 1)
```

- **`IL5RA`** goes down in the tolDCs of both groups, but much more in patients (interaction in tolDC, LFC ≈ −4.3).
- **`ABCG1`**, a cholesterol transporter, goes down from monocyte to tolDC in controls, but goes up a little in patients: the lines diverge (interaction in tolDC, LFC ≈ 2.4).

</details>

## 5. **Step 4:** which processes do they take part in?

As in the previous lessons, we look for enriched terms in each list with g:Profiler (GO:BP, KEGG, and Reactome):

```{r gost, eval = FALSE}
library(gprofiler2)
set_base_url("https://biit.cs.ut.ee/gprofiler_archive3/e113_eg59_p19") # archived version (June 2025)

deg_lists <- split(deg_df$gene, deg_df$query)
gost_res <- gost(deg_lists, organism = "hsapiens", correction_method = "fdr",
                 user_threshold = 0.05, sources = c("GO:BP", "KEGG", "REAC"), evcodes = TRUE)
```

The result is in the `go_interaction_results` checkpoint:

```{r go_interaction}
attr(go_interaction_results, "gprofiler_version")
go_interaction_results %>%
  dplyr::count(query, source) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = n)
```

For the figure we use only **Reactome (REAC)**. To each gene we assign its **specific process**: the Reactome term with the fewest genes in which it appears (as in lesson 4):

```{r reac_specific}
reac_specific <- go_interaction_results %>%
  filter(source == "REAC") %>%
  separate_rows(intersection, sep = ",") %>%
  dplyr::rename(gene = intersection) %>%
  group_by(gene) %>%
  summarise(specific_process = term_name[which.min(term_size)], .groups = "drop")

deg_reac <- inner_join(deg_df, reac_specific, by = "gene")
dplyr::n_distinct(deg_reac$gene) # genes with annotation in Reactome
dplyr::count(deg_reac, query = factor(query, levels = query_order))
```

Of the `r dplyr::n_distinct(deg_df$gene)` genes with a significant interaction, `r dplyr::n_distinct(deg_reac$gene)` have a Reactome process. Those are the genes in Figure 7A.

## 6. **Step 5:** shared and exclusive genes (Figure 7A)

We make a genes × lists matrix with the interaction LFC; it is empty (`NA`) if the gene is not in that list:

```{r fig7a_mat}
lfc_mat <- deg_reac %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, query, log2FoldChange) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = query, values_from = log2FoldChange) %>%
  column_to_rownames("gene") %>%
  as.matrix()
lfc_mat <- lfc_mat[order(rownames(lfc_mat)), query_order] # genes in alphabetical order
head(lfc_mat)
```

We group the genes according to which lists they appear in. We will later use the same function to group the processes in Figure 7B:

```{r patterns}
list_direction <- sub("SLEvsCtrl_(UP|DOWN)_.*", "\\1", query_order) # UP, DOWN, UP, DOWN

# e.g., "NA_DOWN_NA_DOWN" = it is in DOWN_moDC and in DOWN_tolDC
presence_pattern <- function(mat) {
  apply(!is.na(mat), 1, function(x) paste(ifelse(x, list_direction, "NA"), collapse = "_"))
}

pattern_labels <- c(NA_DOWN_NA_DOWN = "Downregulated - SLE both",
                    NA_DOWN_NA_NA   = "Downregulated - SLE moDC",
                    NA_NA_NA_DOWN   = "Downregulated - SLE tolDC",
                    UP_NA_NA_NA     = "Upregulated - SLE moDC",
                    NA_NA_UP_NA     = "Upregulated - SLE tolDC")

gene_pattern <- factor(pattern_labels[presence_pattern(lfc_mat)], levels = pattern_labels)
table(gene_pattern)

# label for each group with its number of genes
gene_split <- gene_pattern
levels(gene_split) <- paste0(levels(gene_pattern), " (", table(gene_pattern), " genes)")
```

Now the column annotations. Each list is identified by its direction, its cell type, and its comparison; above it goes a *barplot* with the number of genes in each list:

```{r fig7a_anno}
column_info <- tibble(query      = query_order,
                      Expression = list_direction,
                      Cell_type  = sub(".*_", "", query),
                      Comparison = sub("_(UP|DOWN)", "", query))

column_anno <- function() {
  HeatmapAnnotation("Expression" = column_info$Expression,
                    "Cell type"  = column_info$Cell_type,
                    "Comparison" = column_info$Comparison,
                    col = list("Expression" = expression_color,
                               "Cell type"  = cell_color,
                               "Comparison" = comparison_color),
                    annotation_name_side = "left")
}

deg_counts <- colSums(!is.na(lfc_mat))
counts_anno <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  "DEG Counts" = anno_barplot(deg_counts, add_numbers = TRUE, height = unit(2, "cm")),
  annotation_name_side = "left")
```

```{r fig7a, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 12}
ht_fig7a <- Heatmap(
  lfc_mat, name = "log2FC", col = lfc_color,
  na_col = "white", rect_gp = gpar(col = "gray", lwd = 2),
  cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_columns = FALSE, show_column_names = FALSE,
  column_split = column_info$Comparison, column_title = "between-group comparison of contrasts",
  row_split = gene_split, row_title_rot = 0, row_gap = unit(5, "mm"),
  top_annotation = c(counts_anno, column_anno()),
  heatmap_legend_param = list(direction = "horizontal"),
  width = unit(4, "cm"), height = unit(20, "cm"))

ht_opt$message <- FALSE
draw(ht_fig7a, merge_legends = TRUE,
     heatmap_legend_side = "bottom", annotation_legend_side = "bottom")
```

**What do you observe?**

- Almost all the genes are **blue**: they go down more upon differentiation in patients.
- The **9 genes shared** by moDC and tolDC are almost all ISGs (`ISG15`, `IFI6`, `USP18`, `XAF1`, `SIGLEC1`...). Patients start from monocytes with a high interferon signature, and that signature is lost upon differentiation.
- The **tolDCs** also have cholesterol synthesis genes (`CYP51A1`, `MSMO1`, `MVD`, `IDI1`, `EBP`), and up-regulate `ABCG1`, which pumps cholesterol out of the cell.
- In moDCs, only `KDM1A` has a positive interaction.

::: {.callout-note}
**Challenge 3.** Which of the genes in Figure 7A are ISGs? Use the `isg_genes` list from lesson 4.
:::

<details class="callout-tip">
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{r reto3}
isg_in_fig <- rownames(lfc_mat)[rownames(lfc_mat) %in% isg_genes$genes]
isg_in_fig
table(gene_pattern[rownames(lfc_mat) %in% isg_genes$genes])
```

The ISGs are among the shared genes and those that go down in each cell type; none is among those that go up.

</details>

## 7. **Step 6:** processes per list (Figure 7B)

We count how many genes in each list belong to each specific process, and leave the cells without genes empty:

```{r fig7b_mat}
process_mat <- deg_reac %>%
  dplyr::count(specific_process, query) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = query, values_from = n) %>%
  column_to_rownames("specific_process") %>%
  as.matrix()
process_mat <- process_mat[order(tolower(rownames(process_mat))), query_order] # alphabetical order

process_pattern <- presence_pattern(process_mat) # groups in alphabetical order
table(process_pattern)
```

Each cell holds a circle colored by the number of genes. We draw it with `layer_fun`, as in lesson 5:

```{r fig7b, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7}
count_color <- colorRamp2(c(1, 10, 50, 100), c("#FDE725", "#5DC863", "#3B528B", "#440154"))

ht_fig7b <- Heatmap(
  process_mat, name = "Genes number", col = count_color, na_col = "white",
  cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_columns = FALSE, show_column_names = FALSE,
  row_names_max_width = max_text_width(rownames(process_mat)), # full long names
  rect_gp = gpar(type = "none"),
  layer_fun = function(j, i, x, y, w, h, fill) {
    grid.rect(x = x, y = y, width = w, height = h, gp = gpar(col = "gray", fill = NA))
    value <- pindex(process_mat, i, j)
    keep  <- !is.na(value) # only cells with genes
    if (any(keep)) {
      grid.circle(x = x[keep], y = y[keep], r = unit(2, "mm"),
                  gp = gpar(fill = count_color(value[keep]), col = NA))
    }
  },
  column_split = column_info$Comparison, column_title = "between-group comparison of contrasts",
  row_split = process_pattern, row_title = "Reactome pathways",
  bottom_annotation = column_anno(),
  heatmap_legend_param = list(at = c(1, 10, 50, 100), direction = "horizontal"),
  width = unit(2, "cm"), height = unit(10, "cm"))

draw(ht_fig7b, merge_legends = TRUE,
     heatmap_legend_side = "bottom", annotation_legend_side = "bottom")
```

**What do you observe?**

- The **interferon and antiviral response** processes ("Interferon alpha/beta signaling", "ISG15 antiviral mechanism", "PKR-mediated signaling") appear in the genes that go down in **both** cell types.
- **Cholesterol metabolism** ("Cholesterol biosynthesis", "Metabolism of steroids") appears only in **tolDCs**, and so does "HDL remodeling", with `ABCG1`, among the genes that go up in them.
- In moDCs, the only gene that goes up (`KDM1A`) is associated with cholesterol transport ("NR1H3 & NR1H2 regulate gene expression…").

::: {.callout-note}
**Challenge 4.** Which genes make up each process in Figure 7B?
:::

<details class="callout-tip">
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{r reto4}
deg_reac %>%
  group_by(specific_process) %>%
  summarise(genes = paste(sort(unique(gene)), collapse = ", "))
```

</details>

## 8. To finish: Figure 7 of the article

We reproduce panels A and B. As in the previous lessons, we capture the *heatmaps* as graphical objects and join them with `plot_grid()`:

```{r figura_7, fig.width = 18, fig.height = 12, out.width = "100%"}
grab <- function(ht, ...) {
  grid::grid.grabExpr(draw(ht, merge_legends = TRUE, heatmap_legend_side = "bottom",
                           annotation_legend_side = "bottom", ...), wrap.grobs = TRUE)
}

figure_7 <- plot_grid(
  grab(ht_fig7a, padding = unit(c(2, 2, 12, 2), "mm")),
  plot_grid(grab(ht_fig7b, padding = unit(c(2, 2, 12, 2), "mm")), NULL,
            ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.6, 0.4), labels = c("B", ""), label_size = 20),
  labels = c("A", ""), label_size = 20, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(0.38, 0.62))
figure_7
```

::: {.caption-justify}
**Figure 7.** Monocyte-derived dendritic cells (*in vitro* moDCs and tolDCs) and associated transcriptional programs, obtained when comparing SLE against Ctrl. **(A)** *Heatmap* of the `r nrow(lfc_mat)` DEGs shared by or exclusive to moDCs and tolDCs, using monocytes as the reference: genes whose change from monocyte to dendritic cell is different in patients than in controls (`DESeq2` interaction term `Group:Cell_type`; padj < 0.05) and that have a Reactome annotation. `r table(gene_pattern)[["Downregulated - SLE both"]]` genes go down in both cell types, `r table(gene_pattern)[["Downregulated - SLE moDC"]]` only in moDCs, and `r table(gene_pattern)[["Downregulated - SLE tolDC"]]` only in tolDCs; `r table(gene_pattern)[["Upregulated - SLE moDC"]]` goes up only in moDCs and `r table(gene_pattern)[["Upregulated - SLE tolDC"]]` only in tolDCs. The color scale indicates the interaction LFC: negative (blue) if the gene goes down more upon differentiation in patients and positive (red) if it goes up more. The number of DEGs in each list is shown at the top. **(B)** Significant biological processes (Reactome; g:Profiler, hypergeometric test with FDR correction) involved in patients in these comparisons. Each gene is assigned to its most specific process; the circle color indicates the number of genes. SLE, systemic lupus erythematosus; Ctrl, healthy control; moDC, monocyte-derived dendritic cells; tolDC, tolerogenic dendritic cells; DEG, differentially expressed genes; LFC, log2 fold change.

The original figure can be found in the [article](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1771959/full).
:::

To save it in high resolution:

```{r save_figure, eval = FALSE}
ggsave("Figure_7AB.png", figure_7, width = 18, height = 12, dpi = 300)
```

## 9. Going further: expression trajectories (Supplementary figure)

In Figure 7A, `r sum(startsWith(as.character(gene_pattern), "Downregulated"))` of the `r nrow(lfc_mat)` genes have a **negative** interaction. If the interaction captures an effect of lupus on differentiation, what does it mean that almost all of them go down? There are three possible explanations, and each one leaves a different footprint on the Ctrl and SLE lines:

| Explanation | What would we see? |
|-------------|--------------------|
| **Baseline difference that is lost** | Patients start from monocytes with higher expression and, upon differentiation, both groups reach similar levels. |
| **Attenuated induction** | Both groups start at the same level; the gene goes up upon differentiation, but less in patients. |
| **Excessive repression** | Both groups start at the same level; the gene goes down upon differentiation, but more in patients. |

To tell them apart we plot each gene's **trajectory**: the mean z-score of each group in monocytes, moDCs and tolDCs. First we select the genes that go down and compute the means, as in `plot_interaction()`:

```{r trajectory_data}
trajectory_genes <- tibble(gene = rownames(lfc_mat), classification = as.character(gene_pattern)) %>%
  filter(startsWith(classification, "Downregulated"))
nrow(trajectory_genes)

exp_mean_df <- zscore_mat[trajectory_genes$gene, as.character(metadata_cleaned$sample_ID)] %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
  pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "sample_ID", values_to = "expression") %>%
  left_join(metadata_cleaned %>%
              mutate(sample_ID = as.character(sample_ID)) %>%
              dplyr::select(sample_ID, Group, Cell_type),
            by = "sample_ID") %>%
  group_by(Group, Cell_type, gene) %>%
  summarise(mean_expression = mean(expression), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(trajectory_genes, by = "gene") %>%
  mutate(Cell_type = factor(Cell_type, levels = c("monocyte", "moDC", "tolDC")))
head(exp_mean_df)
```

Now we plot one panel per gene, grouped by their classification in Figure 7A:

```{r trajectory_plot, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 13, out.width = "100%"}
exp_mean_trajectory <- ggplot(exp_mean_df,
                              aes(x = Cell_type, y = mean_expression, group = Group, color = Group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(classification ~ gene, scales = "free_y", ncol = 6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = group_color) +
  labs(title = "Expression trajectories of interaction DEGs",
       x = "Differentiation stage", y = "Normalized expression (mean z-score)", color = "Group") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom")
exp_mean_trajectory
```

::: {.caption-justify}
**Supplementary figure.** Expression trajectories of the `r nrow(trajectory_genes)` interaction DEGs that go down in patients across differentiation stages (Monocyte → moDC → tolDC) in controls (Ctrl) and SLE. Lines represent mean normalized expression (z-score) per group, with points indicating each differentiation stage. Genes are grouped according to their classification in Figure 7A: down in both cell types (Downregulated - SLE both, `r sum(trajectory_genes$classification == "Downregulated - SLE both")` genes), only in moDCs (Downregulated - SLE moDC, `r sum(trajectory_genes$classification == "Downregulated - SLE moDC")` genes) or only in tolDCs (Downregulated - SLE tolDC, `r sum(trajectory_genes$classification == "Downregulated - SLE tolDC")` genes). The trajectories show that the negative interaction reflects a disease-specific modulation of dendritic cell differentiation. SLE, systemic lupus erythematosus; Ctrl, healthy control; moDC, monocyte-derived dendritic cells; tolDC, tolerogenic dendritic cells; DEG, differentially expressed genes.

More details in the [article](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1771959/full).
:::

Which of the three explanations dominates? For each gene we compare the SLE − Ctrl difference in monocytes (**baseline**) with the difference in the dendritic cell where the interaction is significant (**final**; for genes in both cell types, the average of moDC and tolDC):

- If the baseline difference is larger than the final one, it is a **baseline difference that is lost**.
- Otherwise, if the gene goes up upon differentiation in controls, it is an **attenuated induction**; if it goes down, it is an **excessive repression**.

```{r trajectory_type}
trajectory_type <- exp_mean_df %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(Group, Cell_type), values_from = mean_expression) %>%
  mutate(
    Ctrl_DC = case_when(endsWith(classification, "moDC")  ~ Ctrl_moDC,
                        endsWith(classification, "tolDC") ~ Ctrl_tolDC,
                        TRUE ~ (Ctrl_moDC + Ctrl_tolDC) / 2),
    SLE_DC  = case_when(endsWith(classification, "moDC")  ~ SLE_moDC,
                        endsWith(classification, "tolDC") ~ SLE_tolDC,
                        TRUE ~ (SLE_moDC + SLE_tolDC) / 2),
    baseline_diff = SLE_monocyte - Ctrl_monocyte,
    final_diff    = SLE_DC - Ctrl_DC,
    trajectory = case_when(abs(baseline_diff) >= abs(final_diff) ~ "Baseline difference lost",
                           Ctrl_DC > Ctrl_monocyte              ~ "Attenuated induction",
                           TRUE                                 ~ "Excessive repression"))

dplyr::count(trajectory_type, trajectory)
n_trajectory <- function(type) sum(trajectory_type$trajectory == type)
n_isg_basal  <- sum(trajectory_type$gene[trajectory_type$trajectory == "Baseline difference lost"] %in% isg_genes$genes)
```

**What do you notice?**

- In `r n_trajectory("Baseline difference lost")` genes, `r n_isg_basal` of them ISGs (`ISG15`, `IFI6`, `OAS2`, `RSAD2`…), the difference **already exists in monocytes**: patients start with a high interferon signature and, upon differentiation, both groups reach similar levels. The negative interaction does not mean these genes are switched off too much, but that the baseline difference is lost.
- In `r n_trajectory("Attenuated induction")` genes, all from tolDCs, both groups start at similar levels and the gene **is induced less in patients**.
- In `r n_trajectory("Excessive repression")` genes, the drop upon differentiation is larger in patients.

So a negative interaction can come from very different places: always look at the trajectories before interpreting it.

::: {.callout-note}
**Challenge 5.** Which genes show attenuated induction? Which Reactome specific process do they belong to?
:::

<details class="callout-tip">
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{r reto5}
trajectory_type %>%
  filter(trajectory == "Attenuated induction") %>%
  left_join(reac_specific, by = "gene") %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, classification, specific_process)
```

They are **cholesterol synthesis** genes that control tolDCs induce upon differentiation and patient tolDCs induce less.

</details>

To save the supplementary figure:

```{r save_trajectory, eval = FALSE}
ggsave("Supplementary_figure_trajectories.png", exp_mean_trajectory, width = 14, height = 13, dpi = 300)
```

## 10. Summary

| Step | Key function | What for? |
|------|--------------|-----------|
| See an interaction | `plot_interaction()` | Compare the slopes of two groups |
| Interaction model | `~ Group + Cell_type + Group:Cell_type` | Test whether a contrast changes between groups |
| Read coefficients | `resultsNames()`, `results(name = ...)` | Choose the right question |
| Select genes | `padj < 0.05` and sign of the LFC | Separate UP and DOWN lists |
| Summarize functions | Reactome specific process | See processes instead of genes |
| Interpret an interaction | trajectories with `facet_wrap()` | Tell apart baseline differences, attenuated induction and excessive repression |

### Common beginner mistakes

- **Comparing the LFCs of two separate models "by eye"**: it gives an idea, but not a p-value. To test the difference you need an interaction term.
- **Reading a negative interaction as "lower in patients"**: it means the gene goes down more upon differentiation; the absolute values may still be higher.
- **Forgetting the references**: the main coefficients (`Cell_type_moDC_vs_monocyte`) describe the **controls**, not all the samples.

## 11. Next steps

This lesson completes the learning path. The patients' cells differentiate almost the same way as the controls'; the differences are concentrated in the **interferon signature**, which patients carry from the monocytes and lose upon differentiation, and in the **cholesterol metabolism** of tolDCs. A natural question to explore further is which transcription factors regulate these genes.
